span.p:
SC-004 exception, should
Given The grading reviewer has reported that a requirement names a component. The expert reads the finding and believes it is wrong.

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: When They say the finding is wrong - the word is their domain's own term.

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: The finding is checked against the document rather than defended

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: Where the word is indeed a domain term and not a component, the finding is dropped and the expert is told it was dropped

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: Where it is genuinely a component, the reason is stated once, and if the expert still disagrees their decision is recorded with the dissent noted

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: The grade reflects what the document says after that decision, not what the reviewer first claimed

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: Then A refuted finding the document does not support does not survive into the report, the expert is told so plainly, and a disagreement the expert insists on is recorded rather than re-argued at the next grading pass.
